newsitem.title: LATVIA: FISCAL DEFICIT UNDER ONE PCT OF GDP IN'98,'99.
newsitem.headline: FISCAL DEFICIT UNDER ONE PCT OF GDP IN'98,'99.

text.p: Latvia sees its fiscal deficit no higher than one percent of gross domestic product (GDP) during next two years, the finance minister said on Wednesday.
"Our estimates show that the fiscal deficit will not exceed one percent of GDP in the coming two years," Finance Minister Robert Zile was quoted as saying in a statement.
Latvia's government, headed by the no-nonsense Andris Shkele, has pledged to keep a lid on public spending as the country completes the final stages of its tough transition to a market economy.
"Any changes in the taxation system until the year 2002 will be connected mainly with the harmonisation of legislation with EU standards," Zile said.
Zile mentioned improved state fund management among his ministry's short-term priorities.
"Improvements would reduce the absorbtion of funds into the state sector and result in faster and more efficient growth of the private sector," he said.
